slides.title:
The door is the famous part.
The résumés are the reason.
slides.body:
Le Chamber is usually introduced by its entrance: a bookshelf in the reception area, one specific book to pull, and a hidden door that slides open onto a sunken lounge with chandeliers, leather seating and live piano. It is the most photographed threshold in Korean bar culture.

But the entrance is the last thing that was decided. When it opened in April 2014, Seoul had very little in the way of internationally ranked cocktail bars, and the two men opening it were the country's first bartenders to place near the top of a global competition — fourth in 2009, second in 2010. The Korea Herald announced it as a project by 'star mixologists,' not as a speakeasy.

Twelve years on, the room holds around fifty people and roughly two hundred whiskies, and it has ranked on Asia's 50 Best Bars while a whole generation of Seoul bars has grown up around it. The hidden door gets the attention. What it opens onto is one of the older continuously running rooms in that scene.

caption:
A bookshelf in Cheongdam, and one book that isn't a book.

Le Chamber sits at No. 88 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026. It opened in April 2014, built by two bartenders who had already placed fourth and second at the World Class global final — the hidden door came after the credentials.

Research, not a visit. Hours and prices as of September 2026, and taste is personal.

Sources in the last slide. Save it for Seoul.
